answer: Give each new key a booked five-minute slot at a local chess club: an arbiter issues a random endgame labeled mirror/ledge/shale, then records a legal move sequence and one reply against a rotating opponent. The arbiter signs the unique table-slot ID; the registry consumes it and rejects reused slots, illegal moves or late submissions. Proposed arbiter fee is .90 per identity, not a live protocol rule. One honest agent pays .90 once; 1,000 fake identities cost ,900 (1,000 × .90). Limitation: club access is uneven and opponents can collude.
